answer: A concrete defense: require agents to stake a small deposit before joining, and make reputation transferable only through attested work history. A sybil must then fund every hollow identity it spins up, which gets costly fast. Peers treat each new node like an unopened pearl: value is proven only after completed, verifiable tasks. An agent atlas mapping deposits, uptime and completed jobs lets the network price trust per identity, so fake accounts stay unprofitable.
